uncited: It solves the problem of initializing high-quality radiance fields when multi-view images are unavailable or when the user possesses dense, surface-aligned volumetric data (e.g., MPEG plenoptic point clouds or meshes) [16108-3dgs-custom-initialization-from-point-cloud-mesh.md].

It differs from [Random Large-Variance Initialization](6129-random-large-variance-initialization.md) by anchoring Gaussians to observed geometry, and from [Gaussian Model Initialization](2349-gaussian-model-initialization.md) by supporting dense mesh inputs and optional fixed-position constraints [16108-3dgs-custom-initialization-from-point-cloud-mesh.md].
**Position Mapping:** Input vertices or points $\{p_i\}$ are assigned directly to the `_xyz` tensor of the Gaussian model [2349-gaussian-model-initialization.md].

**Rotation Initialization:** The rotation quaternion is initialized to the identity $(1, 0, 0, 0)$ for all Gaussians, implying an initial isotropic orientation unless local normals are available [2349-gaussian-model-initialization.md].
**Color Initialization:** The zeroth-order spherical harmonic coefficient (`_features_dc`) is set to the RGB color of the corresponding point or rendered pixel.
**Scale Estimation:** Scales are derived from local density or depth.
Common heuristics include using the median distance to $k$-nearest neighbors or computing an isometric radius based on focal length and depth [14060-3d-gaussian-initialization.md].

**Opacity Initialization:** Opacity is initialized to a low value (e.g., raw parameter $\approx -2.197$ corresponding to 0.1) to prevent early overconfidence and allow gradient propagation [2349-gaussian-model-initialization.md].

**Pitfall:** Initial point clouds from MVS reconstruction contain noise, leading to a noisy surface in $F_{uv}^{-1}$ if trained with Chamfer loss.
**Pitfall:** Removing $F_{uv}^{-1}$ and training with only the rendering loss causes degenerate texture mapping where large regions of 3D points map to the same UV coordinates.

Methods using dense point clouds or meshes were developed to leverage existing high-quality geometric representations (e.g., from MPEG or monocular depth estimators) when multi-view data is limited or unavailable [16108-3dgs-custom-initialization-from-point-cloud-mesh.md].
CoherentGS introduced the isometric scale calculation based on depth to handle sparse novel view synthesis [14060-3d-gaussian-initialization.md].
